concept.name: Protocol fees
concept.definition: Protocol fees are all charges and value a protocol collects from its operation — swap fees, borrow interest, liquidation penalties, management fees — excluding the gas costs users pay to the underlying network.
concept.intuition: Fees are the gross till of the protocol: everything users pay in, before it is split between liquidity suppliers, the treasury and token holders.
concept.mechanics: Per DefiLlama's dimensions, dailyFees aggregates all value flows into the protocol's ecosystem (user fees like swap fees and interest, plus yield and staking-derived cuts); it is then decomposed into supply-side revenue (to LPs/lenders), protocol revenue (to treasury) and holders revenue (to token holders). Fee levels and switches are typically set by governance.
concept.failure_modes: Fee revenue can be inflated by circular or incentive-driven volume (wash trading, farm-driven churn) that vanishes when incentives stop; fee-switch promises may never activate, leaving token valuations resting on hypothetical future fees.
concept.misconceptions: Protocol fees are not gas fees — gas goes to the chain's validators, not the application. High gross fees do not imply tokenholder value unless a mechanism routes some share to the treasury or holders.
concept.example: A DEX processing $100M daily volume at a 0.3% swap fee generates $300k daily fees; with no fee switch, 100% is supply-side revenue to LPs and protocol revenue is $0 — flipping the switch might route ~$50k/day to the treasury.

citations.source: DefiLlama docs - Adapter dimensions (fees and revenue)
